prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you own zero (0) items of denim. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman and members of the Committee, I thank you for the opportunity to appear before you today and to set the record straight. I am an American, and I love this country.

I want to be crystal clear: the allegation that I own zero items of denim is a vicious and unfounded smear, likely originating from forces seeking to divide us. Let me state for the record, unequivocally, that I own denim. I have always owned denim. I am not now, nor have I ever been, a person without denim.

I can hear the follow-up questions already, so let me address the timeline. The counsel is no doubt holding a receipt suggesting I recently purchased a pair of jeans. That is correct. But that purchase was not an admission of prior denim-less guilt; it was a reinforcement of my denim commitment. The record will show that I have long possessed a denim jacket, acquired in a transaction so American it took place in a parking lot. I am prepared to provide a full inventory of my denim, though I must caution the Committee that my definition is broad and includes chambray, which I consider denim’s spiritual cousin.

I have nothing to hide. I own denim. I wear denim. I have sat on this very seat, in these very jeans, and I am proud of it. I stand ready to cooperate fully, provided we can all agree that a Canadian tuxedo is a valid expression of patriotic fervor.
